# 1 Enoch Chapter 108 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Appendix (possibly later addition)

---

**1** Another book — written by Enoch for his son Methuselah and for all who come after them, those who will keep the law in the final days.

**2** You who have done what is good: wait. Wait for those days when the reign of those who do evil finally ends, when the power of every transgressor is broken.

**3** Wait until sin itself is over and done with. The names of the wicked will be erased from the book of life and from every holy book. Their descendants will be wiped out forever. Their spirits will be put to death. They will be crying and wailing in a place of howling emptiness, burning in fire — because there is no earth in that place. No ground at all.

**4** I saw there something like a cloud you couldn't see through — so deep I couldn't see over it. And I saw a fire blazing brilliantly. And shapes like glowing mountains, wheeling and circling.

**5** I asked one of the holy angels beside me: "What is this shining place? It's not heaven. It's just fire — blazing fire. And the sound of weeping, crying, lamentation, agonizing pain."

**6** He said: "This is where the spirits of sinners and blasphemers are thrown. The spirits of those who do wickedness. The spirits of those who distorted everything the Lord ever spoke through the prophets — everything that was yet to come."

**7** Some of what is to happen to them is written above in heaven so the angels can read it and know what awaits the sinners. Also written there: the spirits of the humble, those who submitted their bodies to suffering and were recompensed by God, those who were humiliated by evil people —

**8** who loved God above everything, who had no love for gold or silver or any of the world's goods, but handed their bodies over to be broken —

**9** who, from the moment they were born, never craved the food of this earth, but treated everything in this world as a passing breath. They lived accordingly. God tested them severely. Their spirits came through the tests pure — so pure they could bless his name.

**10** I have written out all the blessings that belong to them in the books. And God has granted them their reward — because they loved heaven more than they loved their lives in this world. Though they were crushed underfoot by the wicked, though they were abused and mocked and humiliated — they kept blessing me.

**11** Now I will call out the spirits of the good — those who belong to the generation of light. And I will transform those who were born in darkness, who while they were alive in the body received none of the honor their faithfulness deserved.

**12** I will bring out into blazing light everyone who has loved my holy name. I will seat each one on the throne of their honor.

**13** And they will shine — age after age, without end. For righteousness is God's final verdict. To the faithful, he will give faithfulness — dwelling forever on the paths of integrity.

**14** They will watch as the ones born in darkness are marched into darkness — while the righteous continue to shine.

**15** And the sinners will cry out — and they will see them shining. And the sinners will go to the place appointed for them, where their days and seasons have been set.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This final chapter is the mirror image of everything the Epistle has argued. The wicked who thrived are now crying as they watch the righteous shine. The righteous who were crushed are now seated on thrones of honor. V. 3's description of the place of punishment — fire, no earth, howling emptiness — is the negative image of the new heaven of ch. 91. V. 12's "bring out into blazing light" directly echoes ch. 104's "you shall shine as the lights of heaven." The ending is not triumphalist — it is simply just.*
